uhacca: [U+hana+tvā] (bya) CL=7 To pull out. See - Ūhacca.
uhadanti: [U+hada+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 They defecate. See - Ūhadati. Uhadanti(ti) [u+hada+a+anti] They defecate. See - Ūhadati.
uhadita: [U+hada+ta]  CL=9 One who is defecated, one who is caused to be dirty with feces, one who is smeared with feces.
uhasanti: [U+hasa+a+anti] (kri) CL=7 (A) They smile and laugh softly. (B) They laugh loudly.
uhata: [U+hada+ta]  CL=7 (1) One who stirred up or caused to be smeared and dirtied (as excrement or dust). See - ūhata. (2) One who ascended or rose upward.
uhaññi: [U+hana+ya+ī] (kri) CL=7 He is afflicted. See - Ūhaññati.
uhuṅkāra: [Uhuṃ+kara+ṇa] (pu) CL=7 ["uhu"nti saddaṃ karotīti uhuṅkāro. Dhāna,ṭī.638.] An owl.
uhā: [U+hā+a] (thī) CL=7 Should be abandoned or given up. See - Uhāpohakkama.
uhāpohakkama: [Uhāpoha+kama] (pu) CL=7 The sequence of giving up and acquiring. See also - Apoha.
uhāpohakkamanidassana: [Uhāpohakkama+nidassana] (na) CL=7 (The method) that teaches the sequence of giving up and acquiring. Shows or teaches the sequence of the state of decrease and Increase.
uhāpohanayappavatta: [Uhāpohanaya+pavatta]  CL=9 Arising by the ways of what is given up and what is taken, arising by ways of decreasing and development (Sya).
